summary.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 30% YoY to INR971.8 crore, while EBITDA grew 12% to INR112.9 crore at an 11.6% margin.
summary.overview: Sharda Motor reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of INR971.8 crore (+30% YoY), gross profit of INR216.1 crore (+13%), and EBITDA of INR112.9 crore (+12%, 11.6% margin). For FY26, revenue reached INR3,396.8 crore (+20%), but gross profit grew only 8% to INR802.8 crore and EBITDA 6% to INR419.1 crore. Management attributed the gap between revenue and profit growth to catalyst price pass-through and a suspension business that stayed flat at about 9% of sales, and said new export and lightweighting orders would only show in growth once SOPs ramp. Analysts pressed hard on whether the core business lagged the industry, and management maintained that gross profit growth was in line with industry.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR110.6 crore in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: INR459 crore, incl. exceptional gain INR22.41 crore and exceptional loss INR4.26 crore

segments.name: Emission systems (PV and CV)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue mix: CV emissions 44% and PV emissions 43%. Management called the core emission business steady and is preparing for BS7 readiness.

segments.name: Suspension / lightweighting
segments.commentary: Suspension is about 9% of FY26 sales, flat versus FY25. Lightweighting value market share rose to about 14% from 12.5%, and the vertical is about 10% of gross sales.

segments.name: Off-highway, gensets and exports
segments.commentary: Together about 1% of FY26 revenue, described as growing from a small base.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex guided at INR90-110 crore, raised for R&D in lightweighting, emission-norm readiness and new program SOPs; new facility investments are additional to this range and are tied to customer schedules.

Management expects lightweighting share of sales to rise to roughly 3x FY26 levels by FY28 on FY27-FY28 order book, and expects content per vehicle to rise by INR4,000-10,000 from lightweighting portfolio expansion.
Export margins are expected to be higher than domestic, but after higher working capital needs, net margins are expected to be broadly in line with domestic.
Management expects lightweighting margins to improve as the vertical stabilizes; it does not disclose vertical-level margins.
Industry expects growth across all vehicle categories in FY27; management cited SIAM projections and a steady OEM production plan.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex guidance: INR90-110 crore, excluding new facility investments.
Uttarakhand plant progressing as per plan, close to customer locations for North India; capacity modular and scalable.
Chakan 3 lightweighting plant has started SOP and is ramping gradually; capacity added modularly against customer-packed demand.
Emission capacity augmentation described as straightforward with limited capex; no major capex needed for the export orders beyond Uttarakhand.
Suspension plant is up and running, per analyst comment; management did not dispute this.
demand_pricing: Industry Q4: PV production 15.71 lakh units (+11.3% YoY); LCV 208,000 units (+15.8%); 3-wheeler 345,000 units (+32.4%). FY26 PV production 55.39 lakh (+9.4%), LCV 712,000 (+11.2%), 3-wheeler 13 lakh (+23.9%).

Management said FY26 revenue growth was inflated by higher catalyst prices, which pushed the lightweighting share of revenue to appear flat at 9%. Gross profit growth of 8% was described as in line with industry, which the company said excludes one large PV OEM it does not supply.

Export orders: a new first order from a leading global agri-equipment OEM for Europe (~USD 2 million annual, ~USD 10 million lifetime, SOP Q1 FY28); a test order from a US heavy-industry emission company; North American engine/genset order SOP moved from Q2 to Q3 FY27.
Exports from the current pipeline do not include catalyst content, per management.
Management declined to give the timing of entry into the large PV OEM, calling it a long-term opportunity.

TREM5 for 19-37 kW tractors (~75-80% of tractor market) is expected to open a niche muffler and integrated-muffler opportunity; size not yet estimated, pending design finalisation. Management said this is incremental to current business.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY26 revenue split by vertical and export share?
qa_highlights.answer: CV emissions 44%, PV emissions 43%, suspension 9%, supply chain 2%, off-highway/gensets/exports 1%, miscellaneous 1%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the base business (ex-suspension) grow only 6-7% against industry PV growth of about 9% and LCV of about 15%? Is there share loss?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said suspension is flat at ~9% of sales, and gross profit growth was consistent with the industry (Q4 13% vs ~10%; FY26 8%). It said there was no leakage in customers or margins, and that the industry growth of about 8% excluding the large OEM was similar to the company's growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the North American engine maker SOP been delayed?
qa_highlights.answer: The delay is at the OEM end, which management says it cannot explain in detail; it is linked to inventory build-up from the norm transition. Sample orders start in Q2 FY27 and SOP is in Q3 FY27 for a new launch, not a replacement.

qa_highlights.question: What CAFE III benefit and content-per-vehicle uplift is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: CAFE III is multi-fuel and technology-inclusive, so all powertrains except pure EVs still need emission systems. Management expects an INR4,000-10,000 per-vehicle content increase from the lightweighting portfolio, including torsion beams and subframes.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is planned for the next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 guidance INR90-110 crore, with new facilities for customer needs on top; emission capacity expansion needs limited capex.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventories rise sharply (cash flow statement)? Any supply-chain disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: No supply-chain disruption currently. Inventory rise is in line with 30% revenue growth; inventory days improved.

qa_highlights.question: How do the Donghee TLA and lightweighting margins compare?
qa_highlights.answer: Lightweighting margins described as decent and stabilising over time; vertical-level margins not disclosed. Donghee TLA is India-only (India-manufactured exports included); subframe and torsion beam discussions with OEMs are at an early, long-gestation stage with commercial scale-up over several quarters.

risks_watch: Gross profit growth of 8% in FY26 versus revenue growth of 20% — margin and pricing pass-through of catalyst cost needs monitoring.
North American engine SOP has slipped by a couple of quarters; SOP timing (Q3 FY27) and ramp are open items.
Export orders carry higher working capital; net margins guided in line with domestic.
West Asia conflict: crude, commodity prices, FX and shipping disruptions; management says no current supply-chain disruption.
Regulatory timing: BS6.3/WLTP from April 2027, TREM5 revised draft, CAFE III from April 2027; TREM5 muffler opportunity size still unknown.
Lightweighting share is held at about 9% of sales in FY26; FY27-28 order book conversion is the key test.
Company will introduce SAP and further disclosure on growth drivers over the next couple of quarters, per management.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term growth pipeline and export wins, but defensive and evasive on why core gross profit growth trailed revenue growth. Management repeatedly declined to give vertical-level margins, customer timelines, or market size estimates.
key_quotes: Gross profit remains the better indicator of underlying operating performance and growth was better than industry trends for this period.
So there has not been any leakage of any form in terms of customers or margins.
We intend to approximately add almost INR 4,000 to INR 10,000 in content per vehicle increase because the portfolio enhancement.
This is a test order, but of strategic importance as this gives us entry into another U.S. CV OEM.
